deviations.claim: PACKET.md test 4 prose: "the top face is the hexagon with the corner at (3,3) (the pole)".
deviations.actual: The top face of the tri-filleted box [0,4]^2 x [0,2] (edges at (4,4,2), r=1, sphere center (3,3,1)) is a QUAD, not a hexagon.
deviations.derivation: The two top spec edges (x=4 and y=4) trim the z=2 face at the tangent lines x=3 and y=3. The corner region is consumed by the sphere, which touches the top plane z=2 at exactly one point, the pole (3,3,2) (center (3,3,1), radius 1; distance from the plane is exactly r). The two tangent lines therefore meet at the pole, and the kept region of the top face is the quad (0,0,2)-(3,0,2)-(3,3,2)-(0,3,2): the y=0 edge cut at (3,0,2), the x=4-top cylinder's tangent (3,0,2)->(3,3,2), the y=4-top cylinder's tangent (3,3,2)->(0,3,2), and the x=0 edge cut at (0,3,2). The pole is a regular wire vertex. By the same argument all three corner planar faces (x=4, y=4, z=2) are quads. The test asserts the actual quad with the pole vertex (3,3,2) and the sphere-frame machine-check, and records this deviation. Deviations are expected to be right: the packet's hexagon count does not match the geometry.

Anchors re-derived at HEAD ba04e9c (branch packet/BG-CAD-P7-FILLET): A1 pub fn chamfer( = 1, A2 pub struct ChamferSpec = 1, A3 pub mod rewrite = 1, A4 pub fn new(center: Point3, radius: f64) = 1 — no ANCHOR_MISMATCH. The F1/F2/F3 and F4 constructions all pass the Solid::try_new gate; no happy-path witness failed, so no stop condition triggered.

D3 sphere-frame machine-check (the one open derivation, recorded as required): the canonical `Sphere` carrier subs(u,v) = center + r(sin u cos v, sin u sin v, cos u) (u polar from +z, v azimuthal, ranges u in [0, pi], v in [0, 2pi)). The octant patch of the corner (4,4,2) with center (3,3,1), radius 1 is u in [0, pi/2], v in [0, pi/2]. Its v=0 boundary degenerates at u=0 to the single pole vertex (3,3,2) — a REGULAR wire vertex (verified: no repeated vertex in the wire, and the shell passes the singular-vertices check). The three junction quarter-arcs (each constructible by the revolve arc recipe rotated into its junction plane) map onto the sphere frame as follows: the vertical cylinder's junction arc (plane z=1, from (3,4,1) to (4,3,1)) is the equator arc u=pi/2, v from pi/2 to 0; the x=4-top cylinder's junction arc (plane y=3, from (4,3,1) to (3,3,2)) is the meridian v=0, u from pi/2 to 0; the y=4-top cylinder's junction arc (plane x=3, from (3,3,2) to (3,4,1)) is the meridian v=pi/2, u from 0 to pi/2. Each arc lies on the sphere (|subs - center| = r) and on its cylinder. The sphere patch face is Surface::Sphere with the single closed wire (4,3,1)->(3,4,1)->(3,3,2)->(4,3,1): each arc is the INVERSE of the corresponding cylinder's junction-arc use, so every edge pairs opposite across the two faces and the shell closes. The sphere's natural normal (sin u cos v, sin u sin v, cos u) points into the first octant, i.e. outward from the material at x<3, y<3, z<1; the face is stored orientation=true.

The cylinder wire orientation is not a single fixed pattern: it is forced by the closedness pairing with the adjacent planar faces. The shared machinery uses the wire-position orientation (the trim 'front'/'back' names are per wire position, not per spec-edge end), and the simple path chooses the cyclic order from whether f0's wire-front vertex is the edge's front end va (the (0,0)-style corner, realized cylinder bulging toward -x/-y) or its back end vb (the probe's (4,4) witness). The corner cylinders choose it from the f0 face's tangent use (the tangents map).

The fillet spends no caller budget (rewrite_certificate mirrors the chamfer's). Refusals: empty spec list, non-positive/non-finite radius, partial corner (a vertex shared by exactly two spec edges), or a corner triple that is not the whole spec set -> Refusal::Empty; a non-plane/non-convex solid or >3 spec edges at one vertex -> UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier) at the lift; radius reaching the adjacent extent (r=4 on the [0,4]^2 box) -> Refusal::Empty via the trim's strict-extent check. The H-3/H-4/GATE-3/GATE-4 gates pass: scripts/kernel-gates.sh HEAD reports 'all P-3 gates pass' (GATE-4 unscaled_legacy 111/111); no bare 1e-N literal, no Face::debug_new, no tolerance-migration constructor name, no instrumentation traces in the committed diff. All landed suites pass unchanged (chamfer 9, boolean_m2 4, interior_loop 8, resew 7, cut_boundaries 7, split_plane 10, fillet 8).
